Container.Name: jarvis-workspace
Container.Overview:
Jarvis Workspace: a web cockpit that runs several AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Qwen, Grok, Cursor…) side by side in live terminals on your own projects. You bring the accounts; Jarvis orchestrates.
FIRST START: open the container log. It prints a link like http://<server-ip>:3000/?token=… — open it once and the browser remembers it (the token is also stored in the Data folder, file acceso-token). Whoever opens Jarvis without the token gets a login page: it has terminals, so it is protected on your network.
Create projects in the UI with paths under /proyectos (your Projects share). Link your CLI accounts in Settings → Accounts.

Config.Name: Web UI port
Config.Description: Port of the Jarvis web interface.

Config.Name: Projects
Config.Description: Your code. Inside Jarvis it is /proyectos — create projects as /proyectos/my-app.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Jarvis state: database, access token, account secrets, settings.

Config.Name: Home (CLI logins)
Config.Description: Logins of the agent CLIs (Claude Code, Codex…). Keeps them across updates.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User the container runs as (files the agents create are owned by it). Unraid: 99 (nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group the container runs as. Unraid: 100 (users).

Config.Name: Access token
Config.Description: Empty = a random token is generated (see the log). Set your own value, or 'off' to disable it (not recommended: anyone on your network would reach the terminals).

Config.Name: Groq API key
Config.Description: Optional: free key from console.groq.com for fast voice dictation. You can also set it from the UI.
